name: Unique Visitors
definition: Distinct people reaching a defined marketing or product surface within a period.
caution: Deduplicate across devices carefully; a spike from bot or crawler traffic looks identical to real interest until filtered.

name: Visitor-to-Signup Rate
definition: Signups in a period divided by unique visitors in the same window and cohort.
caution: State the attribution window explicitly; a visitor who signs up two weeks later still belongs in the numerator under most conventions, which changes the rate.

name: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)
definition: Fully loaded acquisition spend (media, tooling, a reasonable share of sales/marketing salaries) divided by new customers acquired in the same period.
caution: Partially loaded CAC that excludes salaries or tooling looks better than reality and cannot be compared across teams that load it differently.

name: Cost per Lead (CPL)
definition: Acquisition spend divided by marketing-qualified leads generated in the period.
caution: A cheap lead that never converts is not evidence of efficient acquisition; pair with downstream conversion rate.

name: Channel Mix
definition: Share of new signups or revenue attributed to each acquisition channel under a single, stated attribution model.
caution: Last-click, first-click and multi-touch models assign the same conversion to different channels; name the model before comparing periods.

name: Click-Through Rate (CTR)
definition: Clicks on a specific placement divided by impressions of that placement.
caution: A high CTR on a misleading placement can depress everything downstream; read it alongside the conversion rate that follows the click.

name: Activation Rate
definition: New users reaching a defined first-value milestone divided by new users who signed up, within a set window.
caution: The milestone must be validated against later retention with real cohort data; an arbitrary action (profile completed, first click) is not automatically meaningful.

name: Time-to-First-Value (TTFV)
definition: Elapsed time from signup to the first value milestone, reported as a distribution rather than a single average.
caution: An average hides the users who never reach the milestone at all; report the non-reaching share separately.

name: Onboarding Completion Rate
definition: Users finishing every required step of the onboarding flow divided by users who started it.
caution: Completion is not the same as value achieved; a user can finish every step and still not understand the product.

name: Aha-Moment Reach Rate
definition: Share of new users performing the specific action that cohort analysis has shown correlates with later retention, within the activation window.
caution: The action must be discovered from the product's own retention data, not borrowed from another product's case study.

name: Product-Qualified Lead (PQL) Rate
definition: Free or trial users meeting a documented usage threshold believed to predict purchase readiness, divided by all free or trial users in the cohort.
caution: A usage threshold is a hypothesis about intent, not proof of it; validate it against actual conversions before wiring it into sales handoff.

name: Trial-to-Paid Conversion Rate
definition: Trials that convert to a paid plan divided by trials that reached a decision point (expired or converted) within the window.
caution: Excluding trials still in progress from the denominator inflates the rate; state whether in-flight trials are counted.

name: Daily Active Users (DAU)
definition: Distinct users performing a defined qualifying action on a given calendar day.
caution: Define the qualifying action precisely; counting every page load makes DAU trivially easy to inflate.

name: Weekly Active Users (WAU)
definition: Distinct users performing the qualifying action within a rolling or calendar week.
caution: State rolling versus calendar week; the two conventions produce different numbers near week boundaries.

name: Monthly Active Users (MAU)
definition: Distinct users performing the qualifying action within a rolling 30 days or a calendar month.
caution: Calendar-month MAU and trailing-30-day MAU are not interchangeable; pick one convention and keep it fixed across periods.

name: Stickiness (DAU/MAU)
definition: Daily active users divided by monthly active users for the same window, expressed as a percentage.
caution: Only meaningful for products with an expected daily-use cadence; a weekly-cadence tool will show low stickiness by design, not by failure.

name: L28 (Active Days per 28)
definition: Average number of distinct active days per user across a trailing 28-day window.
caution: Sits between a snapshot ratio and a cohort curve; still needs the same qualifying-action definition as DAU to be comparable.

name: Feature Adoption Rate
definition: Users who used a specific feature at least once divided by users exposed to (or eligible for) that feature, within a window.
caution: Separate exposure from eligibility; a feature behind a flag or a paywall will show a misleadingly low rate if the denominator is the whole user base.

name: Cohort Retention Rate
definition: Of a cohort that started in period zero, the share still meeting the active-user definition in period N.
caution: Compare cohorts at equal ages (week 4 vs. week 4), never a young cohort's early number against an old cohort's mature one.

name: Customer (Logo) Churn Rate
definition: Customers lost in a period divided by customers at the start of the period.
caution: Logo churn treats a $10/month account and a six-figure account identically; pair with revenue churn before drawing conclusions.

name: Gross Revenue Retention (GRR)
definition: Starting recurring revenue minus downgrades and cancellations in the period, divided by starting recurring revenue; capped at 100%.
caution: Excludes expansion by definition, so a healthy GRR can still coexist with flat growth if nothing is being upsold.

name: Net Revenue Retention (NRR)
definition: Starting recurring revenue plus expansion minus downgrades and cancellations in the period, divided by starting recurring revenue.
caution: Excludes new-customer revenue; a rising NRR alongside falling new-logo growth is not the same story as broad-based health.

name: Customer Health Score
definition: A documented, weighted composite of usage, support and billing signals used to flag accounts at risk of churn.
caution: Expose the weights and their validation against actual churn; an unvalidated composite is a plausible-looking guess, not a measurement.

name: Repeat Usage Rate
definition: Users or customers with a second qualifying usage or purchase event divided by those with a first, within a defined window.
caution: A short window undercounts genuinely repeat users who simply return on a longer natural cycle; check the product's real use cadence first.

name: Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR)
definition: Recurring subscription revenue normalized to a monthly figure, under the organization's stated policy for discounts and usage components.
caution: Not the same as cash collected; a multi-year prepaid contract still normalizes to its monthly-equivalent rate.

name: Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR)
definition: MRR annualized under the organization's normalization policy, typically MRR multiplied by twelve.
caution: A run rate, not a signed or guaranteed backlog; treat it as a snapshot, not a forecast.

name: Average Revenue Per Account (ARPA)
definition: Recurring revenue for the period divided by the number of paying accounts in that period.
caution: State whether the account count is a period average or an ending count; the two produce different denominators.

name: CAC Payback Period
definition: CAC divided by average monthly gross margin contributed per customer; the number of months to recoup acquisition cost.
caution: Uses gross margin per customer, not revenue per customer; substituting revenue overstates how fast CAC is actually recovered.

name: LTV:CAC Ratio
definition: Modeled customer lifetime value divided by CAC for a comparable cohort.
caution: LTV is modeled and sensitive to the churn assumption feeding it; treat a precise-looking ratio from thin retention data as a rough estimate.

name: Rule of 40
definition: Year-over-year revenue growth rate plus profit margin (or free-cash-flow margin), summed as a single check on growth-versus-efficiency balance for a subscription business. A widely used SaaS investor convention — Brad Feld popularized it in 2015, citing a late-stage investor he heard describe it at a board meeting (see [Feld's own post](https://feld.com/archives/2015/02/rule-40-healthy-saas-company/) and [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rule_of_40)) — not a formal academic result.
caution: A young company can clear 40 on hypergrowth alone while burning cash unsustainably; read the two components separately, not just the sum.

name: Magic Number
definition: Net new annualized recurring revenue added in a quarter, divided by sales-and-marketing spend in the prior quarter; a sales-efficiency signal common in SaaS investor analysis.
caution: Distorted by a single large deal landing at quarter's edge; look at a rolling average rather than one quarter in isolation.

name: Net Promoter Score (NPS)
definition: Percent of promoters (9-10) minus percent of detractors (0-6) on the standard 0-10 likelihood-to-recommend question (Fred Reichheld, "The One Number You Need to Grow," Harvard Business Review, 2003).
caution: The denominator includes passives (7-8), who are excluded from the numerator; NPS is a stated attitude, not observed referral behavior.

name: Customer Satisfaction (CSAT)
definition: Share of survey respondents choosing a "satisfied" rating on a declared scale, immediately after a specific interaction.
caution: No universal scale exists; never merge results from differently worded questions or different scale lengths.

name: Customer Effort Score (CES)
definition: Survey measure of how much effort a customer had to expend to get their need met (Dixon, Freeman & Toman, "Stop Trying to Delight Your Customers," Harvard Business Review, 2010).
caution: Scale direction (agree/disagree wording) changes whether a lower or higher number is better; state the wording used.

name: Product/Market Fit Survey Score
definition: Share of active users who report they would be "very disappointed" if the product disappeared, from the Sean Ellis product/market-fit test.
caution: The commonly cited 40% threshold is a rule of thumb from Ellis's own writing, not a validated cutoff for every category or business model.

name: Referral Coefficient (K-factor)
definition: Invitations sent per existing user, multiplied by the conversion rate of those invitations into new active users, for a defined referral cycle.
caution: A K-factor above 1 implies compounding growth only if the invitation and conversion rates hold as the base grows; both typically decay with scale.

name: Deployment Frequency
definition: How often the team ships changes to production within a period. One of the four DORA metrics (Forsgren, Humble & Kim, *Accelerate*, 2018; DORA's public State of DevOps research).
caution: A high count of trivial or reverted deploys is not the same signal as frequent, safe delivery of real change.

name: Lead Time for Changes
definition: Elapsed time from a code change being committed to that change running in production. A DORA metric.
caution: State whether the clock includes queued review and approval time, not just build and deploy time, or the figure understates real lead time.

name: Change Failure Rate
definition: Share of production deployments that cause a degradation requiring remediation (rollback, hotfix, or incident). A DORA metric.
caution: Requires a consistent, agreed definition of what counts as a failed change; an inconsistent definition makes trend comparisons meaningless.

name: Time to Restore Service
definition: Elapsed time from a production incident's detection to its resolution. A DORA metric.
caution: Detection time itself varies with monitoring coverage; a gap in monitoring can make restoration look fast because the clock started late.
